title: A job interview
summary: Daniel has a job interview: talk about your studies and experience, say what you can do with يُمْكِنُنِي أَنْ…, and ask about hours and salary.
intro: After a month as an intern, Daniel is invited to a job interview for a summer post. Today brings the week together: يُمْكِنُ أَنْ… to say what you can do (يُمْكِنُنِي أَنْ أَبْدَأَ, I can start), active participles like مُسْتَعِدّ (ready) and مُوَافِق (agreed), and verbal nouns like التَّرْجَمَة (translation).
objectives: Answer interview questions about your studies and experience
Say what you can do and when you can start with يُمْكِنُنِي أَنْ…
Ask politely about working hours and salary
Accept a job and thank someone

realLife.title: The interview
realLife.story: Daniel irons his shirt twice, prints his CV and practises his answers with Sami the evening before. In the interview the general manager asks about his studies, his experience and his weak points. Twenty minutes later Daniel walks out with a summer job, and the first person he calls is Mr Karim.

sentences.en: I have a job interview tomorrow.
sentences.literal: at me an interview (of) work tomorrow

sentences.en: Do you have experience in translation? (to a man)
sentences.literal: is there at you experience in the translation

sentences.en: I am ready to work in the summer.
sentences.literal: I (am) ready for the work in the summer

mistakes.why: The participle agrees with a woman: mustaʿidda.

sentences.literal: it is possible for me that I start the coming week
segs: it is possible for me, I can

mistakes.why: Join the verbs with an, and the second verb ends in -a: an abdaʾa.

sentences.en: I accepted the job with great pleasure.
sentences.literal: I accepted the job with all pleasure

dialogue.title: An interview for a summer job
dialogue.culture: Job interviews in Egypt are often warm but formal: interviewers are addressed with titles like أُسْتَاذ, and candidates bring a printed CV and copies of their certificates. When someone gets a job, everyone says مَبْرُوك (congratulations).

lines.ar: تَفَضَّلْ يَا دَانْيَال، اِجْلِسْ. أَنَا هِشَام، الْمُدِيرُ الْعَامّ لِلشَّرِكَة. السَّيِّدَة هُدَى تَتَكَلَّمُ عَنْكَ كَثِيرًا.
lines.en: Come in, Daniel, have a seat. I'm Hisham, the general manager of the company. Mrs Huda talks about you a lot.
segs: of the company (lit. for the company)

lines.ar: شُكْرًا يَا أُسْتَاذ هِشَام. أَنَا سَعِيد بِهٰذِهِ الْمُقَابَلَة، وَمُسْتَعِدّ لِكُلِّ أَسْئِلَتِكُمْ.
lines.en: Thank you, Mr Hisham. I'm glad to have this interview, and I'm ready for all your questions.

lines.ar: قَرَأْتُ سِيرَتَكَ الذَّاتِيَّة. أَنْتَ دَرَسْتَ الْأَدَب فِي جَامِعَة فِي شِيكَاغُو، صَحِيح؟ وَلِمَاذَا تُرِيدُ هٰذِهِ الْوَظِيفَة؟
lines.en: I've read your CV. You studied literature at a university in Chicago, didn't you? And why do you want this job?
segs: your life story (to a man) ('your CV')

lines.ar: نَعَم، عِنْدِي شَهَادَة فِي الْأَدَب. أُحِبُّ التَّرْجَمَة لِأَنَّهَا جِسْر بَيْنَ النَّاس وَالثَّقَافَات.
lines.en: Yes, I have a degree in literature. I love translation because it's a bridge between people and cultures.

lines.ar: وَعِنْدَهُ خِبْرَة الْآنَ أَيْضًا. فِي شَهْر وَاحِد تَرْجَمَ مَشْرُوعًا كَامِلًا، وَكَتَبَ رَسَائِل رَسْمِيَّة لِلزَّبَائِن.
lines.en: And he has experience now too. In one month he translated a whole project and wrote formal emails to clients.

lines.ar: مُمْتَاز. وَمَا نُقْطَةُ ضَعْفِكَ يَا دَانْيَال؟ كُلُّ مُتَرْجِم عِنْدَهُ نُقْطَةُ ضَعْف.
lines.en: Excellent. And what is your weak point, Daniel? Every translator has a weak point of some kind.

lines.ar: أَحْيَانًا أَنَا بَطِيء قَلِيلًا، لِأَنِّي أُرَاجِعُ كُلَّ كَلِمَة مَرَّتَيْنِ. لٰكِنِّي لَا أُحِبُّ الْأَخْطَاء!
lines.en: Sometimes I'm a little slow, because I check every word twice. But I don't like mistakes!

lines.ar: هٰذَا لَيْسَ ضَعْفًا فِي التَّرْجَمَة! هَلْ يُمْكِنُكَ أَنْ تَعْمَلَ خَمْسَةَ أَيَّام فِي الْأُسْبُوع فِي الصَّيْف؟
lines.en: That's not a weakness in translation! Can you work five days a week in the summer?

lines.ar: نَعَم، يُمْكِنُنِي. فِي الصَّيْف لَيْسَ عِنْدِي دُرُوس فِي الْمَدْرَسَة. وَمَا سَاعَاتُ الدَّوَام؟
lines.en: Yes, I can. In the summer I don't have any lessons at the school. And what are the working hours?
segs: it is possible for me, I can

lines.ar: الدَّوَام مِنَ التَّاسِعَة إِلَى الرَّابِعَة، مِنَ الْأَحَد إِلَى الْخَمِيس. وَالْجُمُعَة وَالسَّبْت عُطْلَة.
lines.en: Work is from nine to four, from Sunday to Thursday. Friday and Saturday are days off.

lines.ar: هٰذَا مُنَاسِب جِدًّا. وَهَلْ يُمْكِنُ أَنْ أَسْأَلَ عَنِ الرَّاتِب، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ؟
lines.en: That suits me very well. And may I ask about the salary, please?

lines.ar: طَبْعًا. الرَّاتِب لَيْسَ كَبِيرًا فِي الْبِدَايَة، لٰكِنَّهُ يَزِيدُ مَعَ الْخِبْرَة. وَكُلُّ الْمُوَظَّفِينَ يَحْضُرُونَ تَدْرِيبًا مَجَّانِيًّا.
lines.en: Of course. The salary isn't big at the beginning, but it goes up with experience. And all the employees attend free training.

lines.ar: هٰذَا مُهِمّ لِي أَكْثَرَ مِنَ الرَّاتِب. أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَتَعَلَّمَ مِنْ زُمَلَاء عِنْدَهُمْ خِبْرَة طَوِيلَة.
lines.en: That matters more to me than the salary. I want to learn from colleagues who have long experience.

lines.ar: جَوَاب جَيِّد. يَا سَيِّدَة هُدَى، أَنَا مُوَافِق. مَبْرُوك يَا دَانْيَال، أَنْتَ مُتَرْجِم فِي فَرِيقِنَا هٰذَا الصَّيْف!
lines.en: A good answer. Mrs Huda, I agree. Congratulations, Daniel, you're a translator in our team this summer!

lines.ar: حَقًّا؟ أَنَا أَقْبَلُ الْوَظِيفَة بِكُلِّ سُرُور! سَأَتَّصِلُ بِالْأُسْتَاذ كَرِيم الْآنَ، فَهُوَ الَّذِي سَاعَدَنِي فِي الْبِدَايَة.
lines.en: Really? I accept the job with great pleasure! I'll call Mr Karim right now, because he's the one who helped me at the start.

reading.title: Daniel's new job
reading.ar: بَعْدَ شَهْر مِنَ التَّدْرِيب، كَانَ عِنْدَ دَانْيَال مُقَابَلَةُ عَمَل مَعَ الْأُسْتَاذ هِشَام، الْمُدِيرِ الْعَامّ. سَأَلَهُ هِشَام عَنْ خِبْرَتِهِ وَعَنْ دِرَاسَتِهِ. الدَّوَام مِنَ التَّاسِعَة إِلَى الرَّابِعَة، وَالرَّاتِب يَزِيدُ مَعَ الْخِبْرَة. قَبِلَ دَانْيَال الْوَظِيفَة، وَاتَّصَلَ بِالْأُسْتَاذ كَرِيم لِيَقُولَ لَهُ: شُكْرًا!
reading.en: After a month of training, Daniel had a job interview with Mr Hisham, the general manager. Hisham asked him about his experience and his studies. Work is from nine to four, and the salary goes up with experience. Daniel accepted the job and called Mr Karim to tell him: thank you!
segs: to say (lit. so that he says)

quiz.prompt: What does Daniel say is his weak point?
options: He is sometimes a little slow.

quiz.prompt: Which sentence correctly says 'I can start next week'?
What does Mr Hisham say at the end?
options: We will call you next week.
Your salary will be very big.
You must study more Arabic first.
Congratulations, you're in our team this summer!

quiz.prompt: Which word has qāf (ق), said deep in the throat?

completion: Congratulations! You finished Week 10: you can talk about work and study, phone calls, emails and interviews, and you know the main verb patterns. Take the week test, and pass it with 80% to open Week 11.
